title: fix(cli): derive every `os generate` filename from the metadata type registry
body:
Fixes #11071

`os g object customer` wrote `src/objects/customer.ts`. The metadata loader discovers files by globbing each type's own `filePatterns` out of `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, so that scaffold matched nothing and was never loaded — while type-checking, passing `os validate` and publishing without a word. This converges every generator on the registry's declared convention. The predecessor closed it for `skill` alone through a per-generator override; that override is retired rather than copied five more times.

## Measurement first — the enumeration I actually found

Re-derived at the commit this branches from (`2dc0a770`), not carried from the card.

`GENERATORS` in `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` has **exactly seven** entries — `object`, `view`, `action`, `flow`, `dashboard`, `app`, `skill` — enumerated by the `description:` marker rather than by indentation, because template literals inside the map put `fields: {`, `list: {`, `handler: {`, `trigger: {` and `navigation: {` at the same two-space depth as a real entry and a naive scan reads twelve. Exactly one carried a `fileName` override: `skill`. **The card's claim held**: six still wrote `NAME.ts`.

`filePatterns` read from the registry itself and matched with `node:path`'s `matchesGlob`:

| type | `filePatterns` | bare `NAME.ts` | `NAME.TYPE.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | `**/*.object.ts` `.yml` `.json` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `view` | `**/*.view.ts` `.yml` `.json` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `action` | `**/*.action.ts` `.yml` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `flow` | `**/*.flow.ts` `.yml` `.json` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `dashboard` | `**/*.dashboard.ts` `.yml` `.json` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `app` | `**/*.app.ts` `.yml` `.json` | 0 matched | 1 matched |
| `skill` | `**/*.skill.ts` `.yml` | 0 matched | 1 matched |

Zero for all seven, one for all seven. The registry holds **27** entries, and `MetadataPlugin._loadFromFileSystem` (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`) globs **every** one of them by its own patterns — this is the default `eager` bootstrap taken whenever no artifact source is configured. That is the fact that moved the decision: the predecessor scoped its fix to `skill` on the belief that "nothing there is filesystem-discovered today", and the loader does not agree.

## One correction the measurement forced

Three of the 27 entries do not spell their pattern from their own type key: `email_template` declares `**/*.email-template.ts`, `external_catalog` declares `**/*.external-catalog.ts`, and `doc` declares only `**/docs/*.md` and so has no TypeScript filename at all. So the infix is **read out of the pattern**, never interpolated from the type. An interpolated `${type}` would write `NAME.email_template.ts` and re-create this exact invisibility for the next generator added — invisibly, and with every existing test green. A type the registry gives no TypeScript pattern is refused at generation time naming the type, rather than written to a name nothing globs.

## `Clause-②`: **no** — and this is the measurement, not the reasoning

The question was whether pre-existing generated files stop being discovered, which would make this a migration rather than a rename. Measured: **they do not**, because they were never discovered by that path in the first place.

- **Glob path** — a bare `NAME.ts` matched zero `filePatterns` entries *before* this change (table above). Its fate under the loader's glob is identical after: still zero. Nothing is un-discovered because nothing was discovered.
- **Barrel path** — the generator writes the file *and* appends `export { default as NAME } from './…'` to the directory's `index.ts`, derived from the filename it actually wrote. Existing files are not renamed and their existing barrel lines are not touched, so an app loading them by import is bit-for-bit unaffected.
- **`**/*` default** — `filesystem-loader.ts` defaults to `patterns = ['**/*']` when a caller passes none. That matches both spellings, so it tolerated `NAME.ts` before and still does.

No spelling that worked stops working. The changeset and the docs Callout both say so in the user's own terms, with the rename offered as opt-in for anyone who wants the loader's glob to find an old file too.

## The pin is the property, not six literals

`packages/cli/test/generate-file-name-registry-parity.test.ts`. Both halves derived: the roster comes from `GENERATOR_SCAFFOLD_TARGETS` (built from `GENERATORS`, not typed out) and the contract from `filePatterns` read at test time. Nothing in the file decides what a correct filename looks like, and it bites for a seventh generator added later.

It carries its own anti-vacuity guard in the middle. Every generator that exists today is a type whose infix and key happen to be identical, so a `${type}` implementation would satisfy the roster pin completely — the second block asserts the derivation against **every** registry entry with a recursive `.ts` pattern, and *first* proves that corpus still contains a type spelling its pattern differently from its key. A pin that can only pass is not a pin.

## Anti-vacuity — shown failing, with the direction predicted first

Prediction recorded before running. Mutation: `metadataFileName` returns the pre-fix harness rule `` `${baseName}.ts` `` unconditionally.

**Proven on disk** — an editor's exit code proves nothing and a zero-hit `sed` exits 0, so both texts were counted, and the script carried `trap '<restore>' EXIT INT TERM`:

```
### PRE-MUTATION    removed-text hits: 1   injected-text hits: 0
### POST-MUTATION   removed-text hits: 0   injected-text hits: 1
### RESTORE         removed-text hits: 1   injected-text hits: 0
```

Neither leg needed a rebuild and both were checked for it: the parity pin imports `../src/…` and the e2e spawns `bin/run-dev.js` + tsx, so both read `packages/cli/src` directly, never `dist`. (`packages/cli/dist` did exist, built from correct source before the mutation — had anything resolved through it the ablation would have stayed green, and it went red.)

| | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| red | 7 generator cases + 26 registry-entry cases + 2 `null` cases + the `skill` pattern pin + the `object` control = **37** | **37 failed** |
| green | the 13 assertions derived from the written filename or the file's content, which are correct to survive | **13 passed** |

Prediction hit exactly, including which assertions must *not* move: the barrel-line pins stay green under ablation because they check file/barrel consistency rather than the infix, and the parse-probe pins stay green because the mutation changes no template content. Restore leg re-run: **50 passed**, and the restored file is byte-identical to the pre-ablation copy (`diff` clean).

## The contested twin

`packages/cli/test/generate-skill.e2e.test.ts` is on the in-flight `{ ...process.env }` gate's violation list. I own it this round under ruling ①, and its control block had to flip — it was the fence the predecessor put up and this card removes it. It now pins the *other* side of the property, end to end, against the `object` entry's own patterns.

⛔ Its `env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' }` spread on line 117 is **deliberately untouched** — that is the other card's baseline entry. `generate-agent-retired.e2e.test.ts`, the other contested file, asserts nothing about filenames and was **not edited**.

## Verification

Gate set derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` — no hand-built path list. The script confirmed the change set as exactly these 7 paths from the merge base, and confirmed `--repo` against this checkout's `origin`.

Tests, at `HEAD`, after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`:

```
Test Files  4 passed (4)          # parity pin + generate-skill + generate-agent-retired + serve-node-env
     Tests  62 passed (62)
```

The full `packages/cli` suite ran too: **167 of 168 files passed**. The one failure was `serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts`, which spawns the *shipped* `bin/run.js` and needs a built `packages/cli/dist` its own header documents — it was absent in a fresh worktree, and the test passes in the scoped run above once the package is built. Not this diff.

### One gate refused, and was re-run to a real verdict

`check:i18n-coverage` first answered **`COULD NOT MEASURE — 1 of 12 config(s) failed to lint`** — a refusal, not a failure, and its own text says a partial round "says NOTHING about whether any declared label went untranslated". Cause: unbuilt workspace packages under `examples/app-showcase`. Building what it needed (`turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`, `70 successful, 70 total`) turned it into a measurement:

- `check:i18n-coverage` — `OK (12 config(s), 602 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`

That build also unlocked the two ratchets the derivation flags as needing a built closure:

- `check:type-check-coverage` — `OK — 65/78 workspace packages type-checked … 13 in the DEBT ledger`
- `check:type-check-debt` — `--re-measure: OK — 32 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 250.3s, 1897 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number`

### Union re-run after the final commit, at `94830205`

Gate logs carry no sha, so the ratchets were re-run on the committed head with a clean worktree (`0 path(s) dirty`) rather than reported from a pre-commit tree:

- `check:nul-bytes` — `OK (scanned 6492 text file(s) -- 6492 tracked, 0 untracked-not-ignored … no raw ASCII control bytes)`

- `check:role-word` — `OK, no new occurrences of the reserved word`

**Repo-wide, not narrowed:** `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole repo) ran to completion at this commit — exit 0, empty output. No scope reduction is being claimed, so none needs declaring.

## Scope

One card, nothing else. `os init` scaffolds its starter object as `<namespace>_item.ts`, the same divergence from the registry — **not** fixed here and filed unassigned as #11598 instead. It is a weaker finding on purpose: the project `os init` writes declares `objects: Object.values(objects)` from a barrel import, a code-declared load path where the filename genuinely does not matter, so it is a consistency question rather than the silent-strip shape. It also carries its own separate test twins, which is a new verification surface rather than a bounded in-place fix.

Not touched: `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` (generated by changesets; its account of the predecessor stays accurate for that release) and `content/docs/releases/`.
